# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load the Datasets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
dms_data <- read.csv("Tileseq_clinical_predictions_10.28.25.csv")
sanger_data <- read.csv("ABL_Sanger_Gene_mutations_2026.csv")
known_res <- read.csv("known_clinicallyresistant_mutations.csv")
hamming_data <- read.csv("hammingdistance_ablmutants.csv")
probs_df <- read.csv("abl_substitution_probabilities.csv")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Parse Mutation Probabilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clean the probabilities (e.g., "40.70%" -> 0.407)
probs_df$Probability_Clean <- as.numeric(str_replace(probs_df$Probability, "%", "")) / 100

# Create a named vector for quick lookup (e.g., mut_probs["G>A"] returns 0.407)
# Note: Ensure the column name matches your CSV. It is typically 'Mutation.Type' in R.
mut_probs <- setNames(probs_df$Probability_Clean, probs_df$Mutation.Type)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Define Standard Genetic Code
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
genetic_code <- list(
  A = c("GCA", "GCC", "GCG", "GCT"), C = c("TGC", "TGT"), D = c("GAC", "GAT"),
  E = c("GAA", "GAG"), F = c("TTC", "TTT"), G = c("GGA", "GGC", "GGG", "GGT"),
  H = c("CAC", "CAT"), I = c("ATA", "ATC", "ATT"), K = c("AAA", "AAG"),
  L = c("CTA", "CTC", "CTG", "CTT", "TTA", "TTG"), M = c("ATG"), N = c("AAC", "AAT"),
  P = c("CCA", "CCC", "CCG", "CCT"), Q = c("CAA", "CAG"),
  R = c("AGA", "AGG", "CGA", "CGC", "CGG", "CGT"),
  S = c("AGC", "AGT", "TCA", "TCC", "TCG", "TCT"),
  T = c("ACA", "ACC", "ACG", "ACT"), V = c("GTA", "GTC", "GTG", "GTT"),
  W = c("TGG"), Y = c("TAC", "TAT"), "*" = c("TAA", "TAG", "TGA")
)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Engine to Calculate Maximum Substitution Likelihood
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Function to calculate multiplicative probability from one codon to another
calc_path_prob <- function(ref_codon, target_codon) {
  prob <- 1.0
  for (i in 1:3) {
    base_ref <- substr(ref_codon, i, i)
    base_tgt <- substr(target_codon, i, i)
    if (base_ref != base_tgt) {
      mut_name <- paste0(base_ref, ">", base_tgt)
      # Multiply probability if the mutation is known, else probability goes to 0
      if (mut_name %in% names(mut_probs)) {
        prob <- prob * mut_probs[[mut_name]]
      } else {
        prob <- 0.0
      }
    }
  }
  return(prob)
}

# Consolidate unique species and their reference codons
hamming_unique <- hamming_data %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    ref_codon = toupper(first(ref_codon)),
    alt_aa = toupper(first(alt_aa)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate Max Likelihood across all viable target codons
calculate_max_likelihood <- function(ref_codon, alt_aa) {
  # Skip if invalid codon or AA
  if (is.na(alt_aa) || !alt_aa %in% names(genetic_code) || nchar(ref_codon) != 3) {
    return(NA)
  }
  
  target_codons <- genetic_code[[alt_aa]]
  max_prob <- -1.0
  
  for (tc in target_codons) {
    p <- calc_path_prob(ref_codon, tc)
    if (p > max_prob) max_prob <- p
  }
  return(max_prob)
}

# Apply logic and merge back to DMS
hamming_unique$Max_Likelihood <- mapply(calculate_max_likelihood, 
                                        hamming_unique$ref_codon, 
                                        hamming_unique$alt_aa)

dms_data <- dms_data %>%
  left_join(hamming_unique %>% dplyr::select(species, Max_Likelihood), by = "species") %>%
  # Filter out Synonymous mutations (where max_likelihood = 1)
  filter(Max_Likelihood < 1.0)

dms_data <- dms_data %>%
  left_join(hamming_data%>%filter(dose%in%"il3",is_intended%in%1) %>% dplyr::select(species, n_nuc_min), by = "species")

# a=dms_data%>%filter(!fill_value%in%"Sensitive")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Clean Sanger and Define Classifications
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
sanger_grouped <- sanger_data %>%
  mutate(Mutation = str_replace(AA.Mutation, "p\\.", "")) %>%
  group_by(Mutation) %>%
  summarise(Total_Patients = sum(Count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

valid_sanger_muts <- sanger_grouped %>%
  filter(Total_Patients >= 2) %>%
  pull(Mutation)

known_muts <- unique(known_res$Collapsed)
dose_levels <- c("Sensitive", "444nM", "760nM", "916nM")

# Prepare combined dataset
dms_all <- dms_data %>%
  filter(Highest_Resistant_Dose %in% dose_levels) %>%
  mutate(
    Dose_Tier = factor(Highest_Resistant_Dose, levels = dose_levels, ordered = TRUE),
    Observed_in_Sanger = ifelse(species %in% valid_sanger_muts, 1, 0),
    Likelihood_Tier = case_when(
      is.na(Max_Likelihood) ~ NA_character_,
      Max_Likelihood >= 0.01 ~ "High Likelihood (> 1%)",
      Max_Likelihood >= 0.0001 ~ "Medium Likelihood (0.01% - 1%)",
      Max_Likelihood < 0.0001 ~ "Low Likelihood (< 0.01%)"
    ),
    Likelihood_Tier = factor(Likelihood_Tier, 
                             levels = c("High Likelihood (> 1%)", 
                                        "Medium Likelihood (0.01% - 1%)", 
                                        "Low Likelihood (< 0.01%)"))
  ) %>% filter(!is.na(Likelihood_Tier))
# a=dms_all%>%filter(Likelihood_Tier%in%"High Likelihood (> 1%)")
dms_vudrs <- dms_all %>% filter(!species %in% known_muts)
# dms_vudrs2=dms_all%>%filter(!Highest_Resistant_Dose%in%"Sensitive")
sum(as.numeric(dms_vudrs2$species%in%sanger_grouped$Mutation))

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Function to Generate Faceted Plot A
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
create_plot_A <- function(df, plot_title) {
  summary_df <- df %>%
    group_by(Likelihood_Tier, Dose_Tier) %>%
    summarise(
      Total_N = n(),
      Observed_Count = sum(Observed_in_Sanger),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(Percentage = ifelse(Total_N > 0, (Observed_Count / Total_N) * 100, 0))
  
  p <- ggplot(summary_df, aes(x = Dose_Tier, y = Percentage, fill = Dose_Tier)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black", width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(sprintf("%.1f%%", Percentage), "\n(n=", Total_N, ")")), 
              vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
    facet_wrap(~ Likelihood_Tier, ncol = 3) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = "Predicted Highest Resistance Dose",
      y = "% Observed in Clinic\n(Sanger Count >= 2)"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Sensitive" = "#4DBBD5", 
                                 "444nM" = "#F39B7F", 
                                 "760nM" = "#DC0000", 
                                 "916nM" = "#840505")) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none", 
      text = element_text(size = 14),
      axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
    )
  
  return(p)
}

# Generate Plot A1 and A2
plot_A1 <- create_plot_A(dms_vudrs, "Plot A1: VUDRs Only (Faceted by Genetic Likelihood)")
plot_A2 <- create_plot_A(dms_all, "Plot A2: All Mutations (Faceted by Genetic Likelihood)")

print(plot_A1)
print(plot_A2)

Calculating chi-sq statistic
```{r}
dms_all <- dms_data %>%
  # Filter for SNVs only
  filter(species %in% valid_snvs) %>%
  # Filter out missing data / unknowns
  filter(Highest_Resistant_Dose %in% dose_levels) %>%
  mutate(
    # Binarize Predictions: "Sensitive" vs "Resistant"
    Prediction = ifelse(Highest_Resistant_Dose == "Sensitive", "Predicted Sensitive", "Predicted Resistant"),
    # Binarize Clinical Observation
    Observed = ifelse(species %in% valid_sanger_muts, "Observed", "Not Observed")
  )
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Calculate the Chi-Squared Statistic
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create the contingency table
contingency_table <- table(dms_all$Prediction, dms_all$Observed)

cat("--- Contingency Table ---\n")
print(contingency_table)

# Run the Chi-Squared Test (without Yates continuity correction for exact matching)
chi2_test <- chisq.test(contingency_table, correct = FALSE)

cat("\n--- Chi-Squared Test Results ---\n")
print(chi2_test)

# Optional: Print the exact percentages
cat("\n--- Summary Statistics ---\n")
res_total <- sum(contingency_table["Predicted Resistant", ])
sens_total <- sum(contingency_table["Predicted Sensitive", ])
res_obs <- contingency_table["Predicted Resistant", "Observed"]
sens_obs <- contingency_table["Predicted Sensitive", "Observed"]

cat(sprintf("Predicted Resistant Observed: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n", res_obs, res_total, (res_obs/res_total)*100))
cat(sprintf("Predicted Sensitive Observed: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n", sens_obs, sens_total, (sens_obs/sens_total)*100))
```

Spearman correlation between highest resistant dose and number of patients observed having the mutation in Sanger.
```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# 1. Load the Data
dms_data <- read.csv("Tileseq_clinical_predictions_10.28.25.csv")
sanger_data <- read.csv("ABL_Sanger_Gene_mutations_2026.csv")
hamming_data <- read.csv("hammingdistance_ablmutants.csv")
known_res <- read.csv("known_clinicallyresistant_mutations.csv")

# 2. Filter for SNVs and Clean Sanger Data (Count >= 2)
valid_snvs <- hamming_data %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(min_nuc_dist = min(n_nuc_min, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(min_nuc_dist <= 1) %>%
  pull(species)

sanger_grouped <- sanger_data %>%
  mutate(Mutation = str_replace(AA.Mutation, "p\\.", "")) %>%
  group_by(Mutation) %>%
  summarise(Total_Patients = sum(Count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(Total_Patients >= 2)

# 3. Merge Datasets (Isolate Observed Variants)
observed_variants <- sanger_grouped %>%
  inner_join(dms_data, by = c("Mutation" = "species")) %>%
  filter(Mutation %in% valid_snvs) %>%
  # Exclude known resistant mutants to look strictly at VUDRs
  filter(!Mutation %in% unique(known_res$Collapsed))

# 4. Map the Dose Categories to Numeric Ranks
observed_variants <- observed_variants %>%
  filter(Highest_Resistant_Dose %in% c("Sensitive", "444nM", "760nM", "916nM")) %>%
  mutate(
    Dose_Rank = case_when(
      Highest_Resistant_Dose == "Sensitive" ~ 1,
      Highest_Resistant_Dose == "444nM" ~ 2,
      Highest_Resistant_Dose == "760nM" ~ 3,
      Highest_Resistant_Dose == "916nM" ~ 4
    )
  )

# 5. Run Spearman Rank Correlation
spearman_test <- cor.test(observed_variants$Dose_Rank, 
                          observed_variants$Total_Patients, 
                          method = "spearman", 
                          exact = FALSE)

cat("\n--- Spearman Correlation for Observed VUDRs ---\n")
print(spearman_test)
```


```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load the Datasets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
dms_data <- read.csv("Tileseq_clinical_predictions_10.28.25.csv")
sanger_data <- read.csv("ABL_Sanger_Gene_mutations_2026.csv")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Process Sanger Data and Aggregate Patient Counts
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
sanger_grouped <- sanger_data %>%
  mutate(Mutation = str_replace(AA.Mutation, "p\\.", "")) %>%
  group_by(Mutation) %>%
  summarise(Total_Patients = sum(Count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Merge with DMS Predictions and Prepare Plot Data
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
dose_levels <- c("Sensitive", "444nM", "760nM", "916nM")

plot_data <- sanger_grouped %>%
  inner_join(dms_data %>% dplyr::select(species, Highest_Resistant_Dose), 
             by = c("Mutation" = "species")) %>%
  filter(Highest_Resistant_Dose %in% dose_levels) %>%
  mutate(Dose_Tier = factor(Highest_Resistant_Dose, levels = dose_levels, ordered = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Patients)) %>%
  mutate(
    Mutation = factor(Mutation, levels = unique(Mutation)),
    
    # THE FIX: Manually calculate log10 and shift up by 0.5 
    # This ensures that mutations with 1 patient (log10(1) = 0) have a visible bar height of 0.5
    Plot_Y = log10(Total_Patients) + 0.5 
  )

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Generate Waterfall Plot
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
p_waterfall <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Mutation, y = Plot_Y, fill = Dose_Tier)) +
  # Use color = NA so the bar outlines don't bleed together in the long tail
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1, color = NA) + 
  theme_classic() +
  
  # Custom continuous scale that maps our shifted Y-values back to actual patient counts
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5),
    labels = c("1", "10", "100", "1,000", "10,000"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Waterfall Plot of Observed Clinical Mutations",
    subtitle = "Ranked by Sanger Patient Frequency (n = 290 unique mutations)",
    x = "Mutations (Ranked by Frequency)",
    y = "Total Patients",
    fill = "Highest Resistance Dose"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Sensitive" = "#4DBBD5", 
                               "444nM" = "#F39B7F", 
                               "760nM" = "#DC0000", 
                               "916nM" = "#840505")) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = c(0.85, 0.8), 
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
    
    # Hide the x-axis text/ticks because 290 overlapping labels is unreadable
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
  )

# Display the plot
print(p_waterfall)
```
